prompt: In Galatians, what does Paul pronounce on anyone who preaches a gospel different from the one he preached?
explanation: Paul twice says let him be accursed, even if it were an angel from heaven.

prompt: In Galatians, what does Paul say he was doing to the church before his conversion?
explanation: Paul says he persecuted the church of God violently and tried to destroy it.

prompt: In Galatians, where does Paul say his gospel came from?
options: A direct revelation of Jesus Christ, not from any man
The apostles in Jerusalem, during his first visit after his conversion
Ananias, who instructed him in Damascus after he regained his sight
The Scriptures he studied for three years in Arabia before preaching
explanation: Paul insists he did not receive his gospel from any man but through a revelation of Jesus Christ.

prompt: In Galatians, what does Paul refuse to require of Titus, a Greek companion, even though some urged it?
explanation: Titus was not compelled to be circumcised, even though he was a Greek.

prompt: In Galatians, why does Paul publicly oppose Peter at Antioch?
options: Peter draws back from eating with Gentiles when men from James arrive
Peter insists that Gentile converts be circumcised before they are baptized
Peter tells the Gentile believers in Antioch to keep the Sabbath and the food laws
Peter refuses to recognize Paul as an apostle because Paul never knew Jesus in the flesh
explanation: Peter withdraws from eating with Gentile believers once men from James arrive, and Paul calls this hypocrisy.

prompt: In Galatians, what agreement do James, Cephas, and John reach with Paul and Barnabas in Jerusalem?
options: Paul and Barnabas would go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised
Gentile believers would be circumcised but excused from the food laws
Paul would stop preaching to Gentiles until Jerusalem had approved his message
Barnabas would remain in Jerusalem as the pillars' representative to the Gentile churches
explanation: The Jerusalem pillars extend the right hand of fellowship, agreeing to divide the mission field between the circumcised and the Gentiles.

prompt: In Galatians, what does Paul say Abraham's belief was counted to him as?
explanation: Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.

prompt: In Galatians, how does Paul describe the law's role until Christ came?
options: A guardian holding people in custody until faith was revealed
A covenant that annulled the promise made to Abraham 430 years earlier
A means of giving life and righteousness to those who kept it
A permanent standard that Gentile believers must still keep in full
explanation: Paul describes the law as a guardian until Christ came, so that believers could be justified by faith.

prompt: In Galatians, what does Paul say happens to those who rely on works of the law to be justified?
options: They are under a curse
They are justified, but only once they also believe in Christ
They receive the Spirit by works rather than by hearing with faith
They are counted as Abraham's offspring on the basis of the law
explanation: Paul warns that all who rely on works of the law are under a curse, since no one keeps the whole law perfectly.

prompt: In Paul's allegory in Galatians, what does Hagar represent?
options: The covenant from Mount Sinai that bears children for slavery
The free woman who stands for the Jerusalem above, our mother
The church made up of Jew and Gentile together, born according to the Spirit
The promise given to Abraham before the law came
explanation: Paul makes Hagar, the slave woman, correspond to the covenant given at Sinai, which bears children for slavery.

prompt: In Galatians, what two words does Paul use for the elementary principles the Galatians want to turn back to?
explanation: Paul asks how they can turn back again to the weak and worthless elementary principles of the world.

prompt: In Galatians, what does Paul call submitting again to the requirement of circumcision?
explanation: Stand firm, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery.

prompt: In Galatians, what does Paul say the whole law is fulfilled in?
options: Loving your neighbor as yourself
Walking by the Spirit rather than gratifying the desires of the flesh
Keeping every commandment without stumbling in a single point
Being circumcised and observing the feasts and Sabbaths
explanation: Paul says the whole law is fulfilled in one word: love your neighbor as yourself.

prompt: In Galatians, which of these is not a fruit of the Spirit?
options: Self-control
Gentleness
Patience
Enmity
explanation: Enmity is one of the works of the flesh; patience, gentleness, and self-control are all fruit of the Spirit.

prompt: In Galatians, what does Paul tell believers to do for someone caught in a sin?
options: Restore him gently, keeping watch on yourself lest you too be tempted
Bring the matter before the whole church and let the congregation decide
Rebuke him publicly so that the rest will fear to do the same
Separate from him until he shows the fruit of repentance
explanation: Paul tells the spiritual to restore such a person in a spirit of gentleness, keeping watch on themselves.

prompt: In Galatians, what does Paul say a person will reap if they sow to the flesh?
explanation: Whoever sows to his own flesh will from the flesh reap corruption; whoever sows to the Spirit will reap eternal life.

prompt: In Galatians, what does Paul say is the only thing he boasts in?
explanation: Far be it from Paul to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.
